keyPoints.text: Osmosis is the net movement of water through a partially permeable membrane from higher to lower water potential.
Water potential is a measure of how likely water is to move, and solutions with more dissolved solute have lower water potential.
In hypotonic, isotonic, and hypertonic solutions, water enters cells, shows no net movement, or leaves cells respectively.
When water enters a plant cell, the vacuole swells and the cell contents press against the wall, creating turgor pressure.
When a plant cell loses too much water, the membrane pulls away from the cell wall, which is called plasmolysis.

questions.prompt: A biology student says osmosis is just any movement of water across a membrane. Which statement best corrects that idea?
choices: It is the net movement of water through a partially permeable membrane from higher to lower water potential.
It is the movement of dissolved solute across any membrane until concentrations become equal.
It is the movement of water only when both sides have the same water potential.
It is the movement of water only in plant cells because they have cell walls.

questions.prompt: A red blood cell is placed in a solution with many dissolved particles, and nearby water is available to move. What is the most likely outcome, and why?
choices: Water enters the cell because the solution is hypotonic, so the cell swells.
Water leaves the cell because the solution is hypertonic, so the cell shrinks.
Water stays balanced because all concentrated solutions are isotonic to cells.
Water enters the cell because dissolved particles pull water through the membrane.

questions.prompt: A plant cell is moved from pure water into a very concentrated sugar solution. Which change is most likely, and what is it called?
choices: The vacuole fills more and the cell becomes turgid.
The membrane pulls away from the wall, and this is plasmolysis.
The cell wall collapses, and this is diffusion.
The nucleus leaves the cell, and this is crenation.

questions.prompt: How are water potential and osmosis related?
choices: Water potential describes the driving tendency, while osmosis is the water movement caused by a difference in that tendency.
Water potential and osmosis are the same thing, just described with different words.
Water potential is only used for plant cells, while osmosis is only used for animal cells.
Osmosis is the cause of water potential, because moving water creates solute concentration.

questions.prompt: A learner says that in an isotonic solution, water always moves out of the cell because the solution still contains solute. Which correction is best?
choices: That is correct, because any solute outside the cell makes water leave.
That is incorrect, because isotonic means water moves in and out at equal rates with no net change.
That is incorrect, because isotonic means water enters the cell more than it leaves.
That is correct only for plant cells, but not for animal cells.

keyPoints.text: Osmosis is the net movement of water across a partially permeable membrane from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential.
Pure water has water potential zero, and dissolving solute lowers water potential by making it negative.
A plant cell in a solution with lower water potential than its cytoplasm loses water, the vacuole shrinks, and the membrane pulls away from the wall (plasmolysis).
A plant cell in a solution with higher water potential than its cytoplasm gains water until the wall resists further expansion, making the cell turgid.
Animal cells have no cell wall, so in much higher water potential they swell and may burst, while in lower water potential they shrink and crenate.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes what osmosis is?
choices: The overall movement of water through a membrane from a wetter side to a less wet side
The net movement of water across a partially permeable membrane from higher to lower water potential
The movement of solute molecules across any membrane from low to high concentration
The diffusion of water only in plant cells when they are turgid

questions.prompt: A scientist adds salt to pure water and then places a plant cell into the mixture. Which outcome matches the change to the liquid and the cell?
choices: The liquid’s water potential rises above zero, so the cell swells immediately
The liquid’s water potential stays at zero, so the cell is unchanged
The liquid’s water potential becomes negative, so the cell is more likely to lose water and plasmolyse
The liquid’s water potential becomes positive, so the cell becomes turgid

questions.prompt: A plant cell is put into a very dilute solution, and an animal cell is put into the same solution. What pair of outcomes is most likely?
choices: Both cells plasmolyse because water leaves them
The plant cell becomes turgid, and the animal cell may swell and burst
The plant cell crenates, and the animal cell becomes turgid
Both cells shrink because the solution has the highest water potential
Osmosis describes water moving from lower to higher water potential, whereas pure water has a negative water potential
Osmosis is the movement of water down a water potential gradient, whereas pure water is the reference point with water potential zero
Osmosis happens only in plant cells, whereas pure water has no water potential at all
Osmosis is the movement of solute, whereas pure water becomes positive when solute is added

questions.prompt: A student says, 'If a plant cell is in a solution with lower water potential than its cytoplasm, it will swell because water enters the cell.' Which correction is best?
choices: Correct it: the cell loses water, the vacuole shrinks, and plasmolysis can occur
Correct it: the cell gains water and becomes turgid because lower water potential always causes swelling
Keep it: plant cells never lose water because the wall prevents this
Keep it: lower water potential means the cell is in pure water
